ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r6.claim: One explanation is that they give people less of the goods measured or weighed, naming the measure for its contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r6.anchor: قيل : أي لا تنقصوا الناس من المكيال والميزان

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r7.claim: More likely, the warning is against reducing the standard size of measures or weights themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r7.anchor: واستظهر أن المراد لا تنقصوا حجم المكيال عن المعهود وكذا الصنجات

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r8.claim: The parallel passage in al-Aʿrāf uses “measuring” where this verse has “the measure.”
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم في الأعراف ( الكيل ) بدل ( المكيال )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r9.claim: Their present wealth means they have no need to cheat people.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r9.anchor: أي ملتبسين بثروة واسعة تغنيكم عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r10.claim: Alternatively, their blessings should elicit generosity toward people as gratitude, the greatest form of thanks for blessings.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r10.anchor: أو بنعمة من الله تعالى حقها أن تقابل بغير ما أنتم عليه بأن تتفضلوا على الناس شكرا عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r11.claim: A further reading warns that their wrongdoing may make them lose their current prosperity.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r11.anchor: أو أراكم بخير وغنى فلا تزيلوه بما تأتونه من الشر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r12.claim: Their prosperity is given as the reason for the prohibition on shortchanging.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r12.anchor: وعلى كل حال الجملة في موضع التعليل للنهي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r13.claim: If they persist, punishment will encompass them all; the warning may explain both the command to worship and the ban on fraud.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r13.anchor: وفسر المحيط بما لا يشذ منه أحد منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r14.speaker: زمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses “encompassing” as ruinous, citing the phrase about the garden being surrounded by calamity.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r14.anchor: وفسره الزمخشري بالمهلك أخذا من قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r15.speaker: زمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says calling the day encompassing is more forceful: the day contains all events, so its encompassing the punished person entails that the day's punishment has gathered around him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p114/r15.anchor: وادعى أن يصف اليوم بالإحاطة أبلغ من وصف العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r1.claim: Because a day contains all events occurring in it, its encompassing a sufferer implies that every kind of that day's punishment has gathered around him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r1.anchor: والحاصل أن إحاطة اليوم تدل على إحاطة كل ما فيه من العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r2.claim: Punishment encompassing a person may mean only that one kind reaches each person; the day's encompassing implies every kind reaches each person, a more forceful meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r2.anchor: وأما فيما نحن فيه فيدل عل إحاطة أنواع العذاب المشتمل عليها اليوم بكل فرد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r3.claim: The verse's rhetorical contrast is illustrated by a poetic image of virtues gathered in a dome placed over Ibn al-Ḥashraj; the poet is not named.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r3.anchor: إن المروءة والسماحة والندى في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج

ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r4.claim: A scholar explains that the day is the time of all events, so encompassing its victim gathers every punishment of that day around him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين في بيان الأبلغية : إن اليوم زمان لجميع الحوادث

ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r5.claim: محيط may modify عذاب by proximity; another parse makes it modify يوم with an understood “its punishment,” which al-Alusi rejects.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r6.claim: The threatened day can mean either the Day of Resurrection or worldly annihilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r6.anchor: وأيا ما كان فالمراد عذاب يوم القيامة أو عذاب الإستئصال في الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets “good” as low prices and the punishment as high prices.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p115/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وأبو الشيخ عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه فسر الخير برخص السعر والعذاب بغلائه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r1.claim: God sent Shuʿayb to the descendants of Midian.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وإلى مدين} أي: وأرسلنا إلى ولد مدين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r2.claim: They are told not to cheat or diminish measures and weights; they practiced this fraud alongside their polytheism.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r2.anchor: ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان} أي: لا تبخسوا، وهم كانوا يطففون مع شركهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that Shuʿayb saw them enjoying prosperity and blessing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: موسرين في نعمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says they had fertile conditions and abundance.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r5.claim: Shuʿayb warned that their blessing could disappear, prices rise, and punishment arrive if they did not repent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r5.anchor: فحذرهم زوال النعمة، وغلاء السعر، وحلول النقمة، إن لم يتوبوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r6.claim: The encompassing day's punishment will surround and destroy them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p194#2/r6.anchor: عذاب يوم محيط} يحيط بكم فيهلككم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r1.claim: Madyan may mean the descendants of Madyan son of Abraham or the town he built and named for himself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r1.anchor: أولاد مدين بن إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r2.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the town’s inhabitants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r2.anchor: أو أهل مدين وهو بلد بناه فسمي باسمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r3.claim: He begins with monotheism as the foundation, then forbids short measure and weight as unjust and destructive of fair exchange.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r3.anchor: ثم نهاهم عما اعتادوه من البخس المنافي للعدل

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r4.claim: Prosperity makes cheating unnecessary; alternatively it is a blessing calling for generosity, or abundance they should not forfeit through wrongdoing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r4.anchor: أراكم بخير } بسعة تغنيكم عن البخس

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r5.claim: The punishment leaves none outside it; it may be a destructive punishment, meaning Judgment Day or extermination.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r5.anchor: لا يشذ منه أحد منكم. وقيل عذاب مهلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r6.claim: The day is called encompassing although this attribute belongs to its punishment, because the day contains it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:84/r6.anchor: ووصف اليوم بالإحاطة وهي صفة العذاب لاشتماله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r1.claim: After the story of Lot, marked by his obedience without desire or fear and the danger surrounding the angels’ descent, Biqaʿi turns to the nearest famous story in time.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r1.anchor: أتبعت أقرب القصص الشهيرة إليها في الزمن

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r2.claim: Midian is a tribe named for its forefather Midian, son of Abraham; Shuʿayb is called their brother.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r2.anchor: وهم قبيلة أبيهم مدين بن إبراهيم عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r3.claim: Shuʿayb begins, like the other prophets, with the foundation of religion: worship God alone and associate nothing with Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r3.anchor: ما قال إخوانه من الأنبياء في البداءة بأصل الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r4.claim: The prophets’ agreement on one God despite distant times and lands proves their truth, since they did not learn these teachings from one another or worldly reports.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r5.speaker: عمر بن محمد السهروردي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r5.claim: Al-Suhrawardi says the prophets share one source and fundamentals while their revealed laws differ according to divine wisdom and the needs of each community and age.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r5.anchor: قال الإمام شهاب الدين عمر بن محمد السهروردي في كتابه ( رشف النصائح الإيمانية

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r6.speaker: عمر بن محمد السهروردي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r6.claim: Al-Suhrawardi criticizes philosophers for remaining within the visible realm and exposing ignorance and contradiction when they speculate about divinity; he invokes 59:14.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r6.anchor: إن الفلاسفة لما لم يغترفوا من بحار الأنبياء وقفت بهم أفراس أفكارهم في عالم الشهادة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r7.claim: After calling for justice toward God, Shuʿayb calls for justice toward His servants by forbidding their customary fraud in measures and weights, including their instruments.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r7.anchor: دعاهم إلى العدل فيما بينهم وبين عبيده في أقبح ما كانوا قد اتخذوه بعد الشرك ديدنا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r8.claim: Measure and its instrument concern quantity, while weighing and its instrument concern weight or quality.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r8.anchor: فالكيل للعدل في الكمية والوزن للعدل في الكيفية

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r9.claim: The prohibition covers every kind of reduction, whether in what is measured or in the measuring instrument itself.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r9.anchor: لا الكيل ولا آلته ولا الوزن ولا آلته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r10.claim: Their ample means should make fraud unnecessary; the reminder both encourages gratitude and warns that gratitude brings blessing.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r10.anchor: أي بسعة تغنيكم عن البخس - مرهبا ومرغبا بالإشارة للنقمة كما أن الشكر موجب للنعمة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r11.claim: The encompassing day threatens them for both fraud and associating partners, reaching young and old and all their property; it means a destructive punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p563/r11.anchor: بكم صغارا وكبارا وبأموالهم طيبا وخبيثا , أي مهلك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r17.claim: Calling the day encompassing is more terrifying because the day contains the punishment and the punishment in turn surrounds its victims on every side.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r17.anchor: وهو الدائر بالشيء من كل جانب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r18.claim: The image derives from an enemy’s encirclement; Biqaʿi links the same wording to the destruction of the garden in 18:42.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r19.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r19.claim: Ibn Majah reports Ibn ʿUmar saying that cheating in measure brings years of hardship and unjust rulers, while withholding zakat brings withheld rain; without animals, no rain would fall. No grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p564/r19.anchor: رواه ابن ماجة عن ابن عمر

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r1.speaker: ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r1.claim: Rabiʿa ibn Abi ʿAbd al-Rahman argues that the stoning punishment of Lot’s people should not be lifted from anyone committing their sexual practice.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r1.anchor: عن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن الرأي قال: عذب الله قوم لوط فرماهم بحجارة من سجيل فلا ترفع تلك العقوبة

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets Shuʿayb’s seeing his people in prosperity as low prices.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {إني أراكم بخير} قال: رخص السعر

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the surrounding punishment as high prices.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r3.anchor: وإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم محيط} قال: غلاء السعر

DURR-FULL:v4p468/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r16.claim: Shuʿayb began by calling the people to worship God and cease injustice, leaving aside their other wrongdoing.
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r16.anchor: فبدا شعيب فدعاهم إلى عبادة الله وكف الظلم وترك ما سوى ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says God sent Shuayb to Midian and to the people of al-Aykah, a wooded thicket.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r1.anchor: عن السدى إلى مدين اخاهم شعيبا قال : ان الله قد بعث شعيبا إلى مدين والى اصحاب الايكة هي الغيضة من الشجر

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r2.speaker: خلف بن حوشب
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r2.claim: Khalaf ibn Hawshab says Shuayb's people perished over cheating by tiny amounts, taking with heavy weights and giving with lighter ones.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r2.anchor: عن خلف بن حوشب قال : هلك قوم شعيب من شعيرة إلى شعيرة كانوا ياخذون بالرزينة ويعطون بالخفيفة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Midian's people disbelieved and defrauded measures and weights; after Shuayb called them and they rejected him, they persisted and asked for punishment.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r3.anchor: عن السدى قال ان الله بعث شعيبا إلى مدين فكانوا مع كفرهم يبخسون الكيل والوزن فدعاهم فكذبوه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r4.claim: Qatada says Shuayb saw them with an outward coating of worldly possessions and adornment.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اني اراكم بخير واني اخاف عليكم راى عليهم قشرا من قشر الدنيا وزينتها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets their good as worldly wealth, noting that God calls wealth good in another verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2070#2/r5.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : اني اراكم بخير قال : في دنياكم كما قال الله : ان ترك خيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r1.claim: The opening about Shuayb sent to Midian parallels the wording about Salih sent to Thamud in 11:61.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r1.anchor: نظير قوله : { وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا } ( هود : 61 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r2.claim: Shuayb's instruction covers repairing belief, correcting a widespread commercial wrong by not short-changing measures and weights, and avoiding corruption on earth; tawhid comes first as the basis of reform.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r2.anchor: صلاح الأعمال والتصرفات في العالم بأن لا يفسدوا في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r3.claim: Cheating in measure and weight is singled out between belief and general conduct because it was widespread enough that they forgot its ugliness; it combines theft and betrayal of trusting buyers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r3.anchor: إقدامهم عليه كان فاشيا فيهم حتى نسوا ما فيه من قبح وفساد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r4.claim: The prohibition of fraud is reinforced by the positive command to give full measure and weight in the following verse.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r5.claim: His seeing them in good means they are enjoying blessing; he presents himself as a witness to God's favor, for which they owe gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r5.anchor: وإنما ذكر رؤيته ذلك لأنها في معنى الشهادة عليهم بنعمة الله عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r6.claim: Khayr can mean a good condition or wealth; Ibn Ashur prefers wealth here because their resources remove any need to cheat, make the practice indefensible, and support preserving the blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r6.anchor: ويطلق على المال كقوله : { إن ترك خيرا } ( البقرة : 180 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r7.claim: The warning may concern punishment in this world or the afterlife; the wording leaves both open and warns against ingratitude for blessing and disobeying its giver.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r7.anchor: عذابا يحل بهم إما يوم القيامة وإما في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r8.claim: Muhit grammatically describes the day but figuratively means that its punishment will encompass them; the genitive phrase makes this clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p136#2/r8.anchor: على وجه المجاز العقلي ، أي محيط عذابه ، والقرينة هي إضافة العذاب إليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.claim: The wording implies ‘We sent their brother Shuayb to Midian,’ with ‘sent’ understood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.anchor: التقدير: وإلى مدين أرسلنا أخاهم شعيبا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.claim: One view takes Midian as a place, making the phrase mean the people of Midian, as in the idiom ‘ask the town.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.anchor: فقيل: هي بقعة، فالتقدير على هذا: وإلى أهل مدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.claim: Another view locates the Midian region in the area of Syria.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.anchor: وقيل كان هذا القطر في ناحية الشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.claim: A further view makes Midian the name of a man whose descendants formed the tribe; the name is indeclinable either way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.anchor: وقيل مدين اسم رجل كانت القبيلة من ولده فسميت باسمه، ومدين لا ينصرف في الوجهين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.claim: Al-Naqqash says Midian was Abraham’s biological son; Ibn Atiyya rejects this as remote because Shuayb is said to be Arab and Arabs connect to Abraham only through Ishmael.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.anchor: حكى النقاش أن مدين هو ولد إبراهيم الخليل لصلبه. قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا بعيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.claim: Shuayb’s call shows they worshipped idols, confirmed by their later words; disbelief, not sin, merited their annihilation, since God annihilates no nation except for disbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.anchor: ودعاء «شعيب» إلى «عبادة الله» يقتضي أنهم كانوا يعبدون الأوثان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r7.claim: They agreed to give outsiders short measure and weight while taking full measure from them; accompanying sin was secondary to their disbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r7.anchor: أن يأخذوا ممن يرد عليهم من غيرهم وافيا ويعطوا ناقصا في وزنهم وكيلهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r8.claim: Zajjaj’s book suggests that the people had agreed among themselves to defraud one another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r8.anchor: ويظهر من كتاب الزجاج أنهم كانوا تراضوا بينهم بأن يبخس بعضهم بعضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ‘in prosperity’ as low prices and the encompassing day’s punishment as ruinous high prices.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: معناه في رخص من الأسعار، و «عذاب اليوم المحيط» هو حلول الغلاء المهلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r10.claim: The Prophet said that whenever a people short-measure and short-weigh, their provision is withheld; Ibn Atiyya cites this in support, without grading it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r10.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما نقص قوم المكيال والميزان إلا ارتفع عنهم الرزق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r11.claim: Another view takes ‘good’ as all God’s blessings and the punishment as the destruction that ultimately befell them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p198#2/r11.anchor: وقيل لهم قوله: بخير عام في جميع نعم الله تعالى، و «عذاب اليوم» هو الهلاك الذي حل بهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p199/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p199/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p199/r1.claim: Calling the day encompassing is figurative because the punishment occurs on that day; alternatively, the day is encompassing because its evil surrounds them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p199/r1.anchor: ووصف «اليوم» ب «الإحاطة» وهي من صفة العذاب على جهة التجوز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī refers the account of Midian to his earlier explanation at al-Aʿrāf 85.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وإلى مدين ﴾ قد ذكرناه في ( الأعراف 85 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r2.claim: Shuʿayb forbids short measure and weight; his people practiced fraud despite their unbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r2.anchor: أي لاتطففوا وكانوا يطففون مع كفرهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r3.speaker: ابن العباس والحسن ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid understand their good condition as low prices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه رخص الأسعار قاله ابن العباس والحسن ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās, along with Qatāda and Ibn Zayd, takes it as abundant wealth; al-Farrāʾ notes they had much wealth and cheap prices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r4.anchor: والثاني سعة المال وهو مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا وبه قال قتادة وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ argues that their plentiful wealth and low prices left them no need to cheat in weighing and measuring.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء أموالكم كثيرة وأسعاركم رخيصة فأي حاجة بكم إلى سوء الوزن والكيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the encompassing punishment is high prices; Mujāhid specifies drought, famine, and high prices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r6.anchor: أحدها أنه غلاء السعر قاله ابن عباس وقال مجاهد القحط والجدب والغلاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r7.claim: Muqātil says the threat is a worldly punishment, the one that later struck them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r7.anchor: والثاني العذاب في الدنيا وهوالذي أصابهم قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r8.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r8.claim: Al-Māwardī gives the third interpretation: the punishment of the Fire in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p147/r8.anchor: والثالث عذاب النار في الآخرة ذكره الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r1.claim: Madyan was an Arab tribe living between the Hijaz and Syria near Ma'an, in a place named after them; Shu'ayb was sent to them and had one of their noblest lineages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r1.anchor: وهم قبيلة من العرب، كانوا يسكنون بين الحجاز والشام، قريبا من بلاد معان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r2.claim: Shu'ayb calls his people to worship God alone and forbids cheating in measure and weight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r2.anchor: يأمرهم بعبادة الله تعالى وحده، وينهاهم عن التطفيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir understands their being in good as having a favorable livelihood and provision; he fears God's sanctities will be violated and their prosperity taken away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r3.anchor: أي: في معيشتكم ورزقكم فأخاف أن تسلبوا ما أنتم فيه بانتهاككم محارم الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r4.claim: The encompassing day's punishment refers to punishment in the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p342/r4.anchor: عذاب يوم محيط} (11) أي: في الدار الآخرة

JISHUMI:v5p3548/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3548/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3548/r5.claim: Muhit describes something encircling another like a wall; the related verb can also mean to contain or surround with care.
JISHUMI:v5p3548/r5.anchor: المحيط: الدائر على الشيء بمثل الحائط، أحاط به يحيط إحاطة، فهو محيط، وحاطه يحوطه حوطا

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r1.claim: Shu'ayb is called their brother in kinship; Madyan may refer to the descendants of Midian son of Abraham.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r1.anchor: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا أي: فأرسلنا إلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا في النسب، قيل: ولد مدين بن إبراهيم، فنسبوا إليه

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r2.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Madyan is the name of a city or a tribe.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم للمدينة أو القبيلة، عن الزجاج

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r3.claim: Abu Muslim says Madyan is the city's name, with its people intended.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r3.anchor: وقيل: اسم للمدينة وأراد إلى أهلها، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r4.claim: Worship Allah means affirm His oneness and worship no other; the passage begins with tawhid because it is the most important duty and the foundation of the rest.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r4.anchor: قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله أي: وحدوه ولا تعبدوا معه غيره ما لكم من إله غيره تقديره: ما لكم إله غيره، فبدأ بالتوحيد؛ لأنه أهم

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r5.claim: They are forbidden to give short measure or weight in what they sell to others; they had been cheating in those transactions.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r5.anchor: ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان أي: لا تنقصوا ما كلتم ووزنتم على غيركم، وكانوا يطففون في ذلك، فنهوا عنه

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan interpret their being in good as low prices; Shu'ayb warns that prices may rise, blessings disappear, and punishment arrive.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r6.anchor: إني أراكم بخير قيل: برخص الأسعار، فحذرهم غلاءها، وزوال النعمة، وحلول النقمة، عن ابن عباس، والحسن

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r7.speaker: قتادة، وابن زيد، والضحاك
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r7.claim: Qatada, Ibn Zayd, and al-Dahhak take the good to mean wealth and worldly adornment.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r7.anchor: وقيل: المال، وزينة الدنيا، عن قتادة، وابن زيد، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r8.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r8.claim: Mujahid understands their good condition as fertility and abundance.

JISHUMI:v5p3549/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r9.claim: The punishment will envelop them all so that none escape; the day surrounds them with punishment instead of the blessings that currently surround them.
JISHUMI:v5p3549/r9.anchor: يعني: عذاب اليوم يحيط بكم، وقيل: اليوم يحيط بعذابه بدلا من إحاطته بنعمته، وأراد بالإحاطة أنه يهلكهم جميعا، فلا ينجو منهم أحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r1.claim: Shuʿayb may mean they possess ample wealth and therefore need not cheat in measures.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r1.anchor: يريد : بثروة واسعة تغنيكم عن التطفيف .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they enjoy God's blessing, which should be met with conduct other than fraud.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r2.anchor: أو أراكم بنعمة من الله حقها أن تقابل بغير ما تفعلون .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, they are already in a good state and should not destroy it through their conduct, as in the speech of Pharaoh's believing man (40:29).
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r3.anchor: أو أراكم بخير فلا تزيلوه عنكم بما أنتم عليه ، كقول مؤمن آل فرعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r4.claim: A day encompassing them is a destructive day; the wording echoes the destruction of the garden in 18:42 and originally evokes enemy encirclement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r4.anchor: مهلك من قوله : { وأحيط بثمره } ( الكهف : 42 ) وأصله من إحاطة العدو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r5.claim: Calling the day encompassing is more forceful than calling the punishment so, because the day contains events and its encompassing torment gathers all it contains upon the sufferer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p393#2/r5.anchor: قلت : بل وصف اليوم بها ، لأن اليوم زمان يشتمل على الحوادث ، فإذا أحاط بعذابه فقد اجتمع

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r1.claim: Madyan here is the people of Shuʿayb.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r2.claim: One account says they are the sons of Madyan son of Abraham; the tribal ancestor’s name stands for his descendants, as with Muḍar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r2.anchor: لأنهم بنو مدين بن إبراهيم , فقيل مدين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r3.claim: Another account identifies Madyan as their city, whose name was used for its inhabitants for brevity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r3.anchor: أن مدين اسم مدينتهم فنسبوا إليها ثم اقتصر على اسم المدينة تخفيفا

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r4.claim: Madyan may be a foreign name or, alternatively, an Arabic one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r4.anchor: أنه اسم أعجمي . الثاني : أنه اسم عربي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r5.claim: If it is a city name, it may derive from madana, “to reside in a place,” with the yāʾ treated as extra.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r5.anchor: مدن بالمكان إذا أقام فيه , والياء زائدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r6.claim: If it is a man’s name, it may derive from dānat, “to rule or possess,” with the mīm treated as extra.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r6.anchor: دينت أي ملكت والميم زائدمة , وهذا قول من زعم أنه اسم رجل

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r7.claim: Shuʿayb is a diminutive of shaʿb, which can mean a mountain path.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r7.anchor: شعيب فتصغير شعب وفيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أنه الطريق في الجبل

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r8.claim: Another proposed sense of shaʿb is a great tribe.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r9.claim: A third proposal derives the name from repairing a broken vessel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r9.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من شعب الإناء المكسور

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r10.claim: Though guilty of shirk, they also cheated in measures; belief calls them to abandon shirk and full measure forbids cheating.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r10.anchor: كانوا مع كفرهم أهل بخس وتطفيف فأمروا بالإيمان إقلاعا عن الشرك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan take “in good condition” to mean low prices.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r11.anchor: أنه رخص السعر , قاله ابن عباس والحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r12.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r12.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take it to mean wealth and worldly adornment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r12.anchor: أنه المال وزينة الدنيا , قال قتادة وابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r13.claim: A further possible sense is abundant crops and earnings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r13.anchor: ويحتمل تأويلا ثالثا : أنه الخصب والكسب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r14.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r14.claim: On the low-price reading of “in good condition,” the warning can mean fear of high prices.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r14.anchor: غلاء السعر , وهو مقتضى قول ابن عباس والحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r15.claim: Another possibility is worldly punishment of total destruction.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p494/r16.claim: The warning can also mean the punishment of the Fire in the afterlife.

MUQATIL:11:84-85/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r1.claim: Midyan was a son of Abraham, and Shuayb was son of Nuwayb, son of Midyan, son of Abraham.

MUQATIL:11:84-85/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r2.claim: God sent Shuayb to Midyan; calling him their brother describes kinship, not shared religion.
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r2.anchor: يعني أرسلنا، { أخاهم شعيبا } ، وليس بأخيهم في الدين

MUQATIL:11:84-85/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r3.claim: Worship God means affirm His oneness; they have no lord other than Him.
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r3.anchor: يعني وحدوا الله، { ما لكم من إله غيره }

MUQATIL:11:84-85/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r4.claim: Shuayb forbids short measure and weight when they measure and weigh; they are prosperous and blessed, yet he fears worldly punishment that will encompass them all.
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r4.anchor: ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان } إذا كلتم ووزنتم

MUQATIL:11:84-85/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r5.claim: The encompassing day means punishment surrounded them so completely that none escaped.
MUQATIL:11:84-85/r5.anchor: يعني أحاط بهم العذاب، فلم ينج منهم أحد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r1.claim: Madyan is either the town or its eponymous ancestor, Madyan son of Abraham; Shuaib was sent to its residents or descendants.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r1.anchor: هو اسم مدينتهم أو اسم جدهم مدين بن إبراهيم أى وارسلنا شعيبا إلى ساكنى مدين أو إلى بنى مدين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r2.claim: Do not short the measure of measured goods or the balance of weighed goods.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r2.anchor: أى المكيال بالمكيال ﴿ والميزان ﴾ والموزون بالميزان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r3.claim: He sees them as wealthy enough not to cheat, or blessed by God and obliged to respond with better conduct.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r3.anchor: بثروة وسعة تغنيكم عن التطفيف أو اراكم بنعمة من الله حقها أن تقابل بغير ما تفعلون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r4.claim: The encompassing punishment means worldly extermination or afterlife punishment, evoking an enemy's siege.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167/r4.anchor: مهلك من قوله وأحيط بثمره وأصله من إحاطة العدو والمراد عذاب الاستئصال فى الدنيا أو عذاب الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r1.claim: Shuʿayb was sent to Madyan, the people of Shuʿayb.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r1.anchor: أي وأرسلنا إلى مدين، ومدين هم قوم شعيب

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r2.claim: One view identifies Madyan as the descendants of Madyan son of Abraham, using the name for his offspring as Mudar can mean the descendants of Mudar.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنهم بنو مدين بن إبراهيم فقيل: مدين والمراد بنو مدين

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r3.claim: A second view takes Madyan as the name of their city, from which its inhabitants were named.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r3.anchor: الثاني أنه اسم مدينتهم، فنسبوا إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r4.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says Madyan is indeclinable because it is a city name.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: لا ينصرف مدين لأنه اسم مدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r5.claim: They cheated when buying and selling: they took excess measure from food sellers but gave food buyers short measure, so they were commanded to abandon shirk and fraud.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r5.anchor: كانوا مع كفرهم أهل بخس وتطفيف كانوا إذا جاءهم البائع بالطعام

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r6.claim: When buying they demanded the greatest possible measure, but when selling they gave less and withheld as much as possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r6.anchor: أخذوا بكيل زائد، واستوفوا بغاية ما يقدرون عليه وظلموا وإن جاءهم مشتر للطعام

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r7.claim: The command to worship God makes them leave shirk, while the command to fulfill measure makes them leave cheating.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r7.anchor: فأمروا بالإيمان إقلاعا عن الشرك، وبالوفاء نهيا عن التطفيف

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r8.claim: Shuʿayb sees them enjoying ample provision and many blessings.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r8.anchor: أي في سعة من الرزق، وكثرة من النعم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says their good circumstances meant prices were low.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r10.claim: Calling the day encompassing means its punishment will surround them, like calling a day severe to mean its heat is severe.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r10.anchor: وصف اليوم بالإحاطة، وأراد وصف ذلك اليوم بالإحاطة بهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r11.claim: One view identifies the punishment as the fire of the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r11.anchor: واختلف في ذلك العذاب فقيل: هو عذاب النار في الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r12.claim: Another view identifies it as earthly destruction.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r13.claim: A third view, related from Ibn ʿAbbās, takes the punishment to mean high prices.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r13.anchor: وقيل: غلاء السعر روي معناه عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r14.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r14.claim: The Prophet said that when a people openly cheat in measure and weight, God afflicts them with drought and high prices; no grading is given.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-86/r14.anchor: ما أظهر قوم البخس في المكيال والميزان إلا ابتلاهم الله بالقحط والغلاء

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r1.claim: In an admonitory exchange, a ruler's excuses blaming servants for trampling crops, drinking wine, and wearing forbidden finery are rejected: rulers themselves abused power, disobeyed, and risked bringing calamity on their host despite God's many blessings.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r1.anchor: ليس كما تقول يا ابن مروان ، ولكنكم قوم ملكتم فظلمتم وتركتم ما أمرتم فأذاقكم الله وبال أمركم

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r2.claim: A Persian couplet says humility is praiseworthy from the exalted, while humility from a beggar is simply his natural condition.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r2.anchor: تواضع زكردن فرازان نكوست كدا كر تواضع كند خوى اوست

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r3.claim: Injustice grows with the hardness allotted to each heart; once hardness surrounds the heart's mirror, salvation is unlikely, so one should seek protection from tyranny and guidance to justice.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r3.anchor: الظلم من نتائج القساوة التي تمطر على كل قلب مقدار ما قدر له فلا يزال يزداد ظلم المرء بحسب ازدياد قساوة قلبه

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r4.claim: Midian may be Abraham's son, whose name later designated the tribe, or the city built by Midian and named after him; the address means the tribe or city's inhabitants.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r4.anchor: هو اسم ابن إبراهيم عليه السلام ثم صار اسما للقبيلة ، أو اسم مدينة بناها مدين فسميت باسمه ، أي : وأرسلنا إلى قبيلة مدين

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r5.claim: Shuʿayb is called their brother because he belonged to them by lineage.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r5.anchor: أخاهم أي : واحدا منهم في النسب.

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r6.claim: شعيبا is an appositional clarification; Shuʿayb is identified as son of Mikayil, Yashjar, and Midian.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r6.anchor: شعيبا عطف بيان له وهو ابن ميكيل بن يشجر بن مدين

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r7.claim: قال introduces an explanatory answer to an implicit question.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r7.anchor: قال استئناف بياني يا قوم (اي كروه من) اعبدوا الله وحده ولا تشركوا به شيئا من الأصنام

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r8.claim: Shuʿayb calls them to worship God alone and associate nothing with Him, since there is no deity besides Him.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r8.anchor: لأنه مالكم من إله غيره أي : ليس لكم إله سوى الله تعالى وكانت كلمة جميع الأنبياء في التوحيد واحدة

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r9.claim: Every prophet's message on monotheism was one, calling people to the one God and worship of Him; Shuʿayb begins with tawhid as the foundation of the whole matter.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r9.anchor: وكانت كلمة جميع الأنبياء في التوحيد واحدة فدعوا إلى الله الواحد

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r10.claim: After commanding monotheism, Shuʿayb forbids their habitual short measure and weight because it brings ruin.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r10.anchor: ثم نهاهم عما اعتادوه من النقص في الكيل والوزن لأنه يورث الهلاك

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r11.claim: The terms denote measures and weighing instruments; Midianites kept two of each, using larger measures when taking and smaller ones when giving.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r11.anchor: وكان لهم مكيالان وميزانان أحدهما أكبر من الآخر فإذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون بالأكبر ، وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون بالأصغر

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r12.claim: The prohibition also covers reducing a measure's capacity or altering weights to deprive people of their rights; the author says this fraud still persists.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r12.anchor: والمراد لا تنقصوا حجم المكيال عن المعهود ، وكذا الصنجات كي تتوسلوا بذلك إلى بخس حقوق الناس

BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r13.claim: Shuʿayb gives their prosperity and abundance as the reason they have no need to cheat.
BURSEVI:v4p107#2/r13.anchor: إني أرايكم بخير علة للنهي أي : ملتبسين بثروة وسعة تغنيكم عن التطفيف.

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r1.claim: This is the sixth narrative recounted in the sūra.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r1.anchor: اعلم أن هذا هو القصة السادسة من القصص المذكورة في هذه السورة

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r2.claim: Madyan was Abraham’s son, whose name later denoted the tribe; on this reading, the verse addresses the people of Madyan.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r2.anchor: مدين اسم ابن لإبراهيم عليه السلام ، ثم صار اسما للقبيلة

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r3.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r3.claim: Many exegetes identify Madyan as a city founded by Madyan son of Abraham; the verse then omits أهل, meaning its inhabitants.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r3.anchor: وكثير من المفسرين يذهب إلى أن مدين اسم مدينة بناها مدين بن إبراهيم عليه السلام والمعنى على هذا التقدير : وأرسلنا إلى أهل مدين فحذف الأهل

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r4.claim: Prophets begin by calling people to monotheism, then address the next most pressing matter; Shuʿayb accordingly first called them to worship God alone.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r4.anchor: الأنبياء عليهم السلام يشرعون في أول الأمر بالدعوة إلى التوحيد ، فلهذا قال شعيب عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r5.claim: Because short measure was customary in Madyan, Shuʿayb next forbade it; the wrong could be giving less when measuring for others or taking more than due, both reducing another’s right.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r5.anchor: ولما كان المعتاد من أهل مدين البخس في المكيال والميزان ، دعاهم إلى ترك هذه العادة

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r6.claim: One reading is a warning that prices will rise and blessing disappear unless they repent of cheating.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r6.anchor: أنه حذرهم من غلاء السعر وزوال النعمة إن لم يتوبوا

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r7.claim: Alternatively, God has already granted them wealth, low prices, and abundance, so they have no need to cheat in measure.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r7.anchor: أنه تعالى أتاكم بالخير الكثير والمال والرخص والسعة فلا حاجة بكم إلى هذا التطفيف

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets ‘I fear’ as ‘I know’: the encompassing punishment will occur.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أخاف أي أعلم حصول عذاب يوم محيط

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r9.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r9.claim: Others take it as genuine fear: because they may abandon the practice from fear of punishment, Shuʿayb’s statement expresses expectation rather than certain knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد هو الخوف ، لأنه يجوز أن يتركوا ذلك العمل خشية أن يحصل لهم العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r10.claim: The day is grammatically described as encompassing, while the punishment is what it encompasses by metaphor, as in 11:77.
RAZI-FULL:v18p33/r10.anchor: والمحيط من صفة اليوم في الظاهر ، وفي المعنى من صفة العذاب وذلك مجاز مشهور كقوله : { هاذا يوم عصيب }

RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r1.claim: One view identifies the encompassing punishment as the Day of Resurrection, appointed for the punishment of the condemned.
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r1.anchor: فقال بعضهم : هو عذاب يوم القيامة ، لأنه اليوم الذي نصب لإحاطة العذاب بالمعذبين

RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r2.claim: Another view includes punishment in both this world and the next.
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل يدخل فيه عذاب الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r3.claim: A third view means the worldly punishment of total destruction, as for other prophets’ peoples.
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل المراد منه عذاب الاستئصال في الدنيا كما في حق سائر الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r4.claim: Al-Razi says the phrase encompasses every punishment, surrounding them from every side like a circle surrounds what is inside; this intensifies the threat, as in 18:42.
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r4.anchor: والأقرب دخول كل عذاب فيه وإحاطة العذاب بهم كإحاطة الدائرة بما في داخلها فينالهم من كل وجه وذلك مبالغة في الوعد

RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r5.claim: Repeating the command is emphatic because the people persisted in the cheating and needed strong insistence.
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r5.anchor: أن القوم كانوا مصرين على ذلك العمل فاحتج في المنع منه إلى المبالغة والتأكيد

RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r6.claim: Forbidding short measure and commanding full measure are distinct; joining prohibition and its opposite’s command reinforces the warning, like commanding kinship and forbidding severance.
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r6.anchor: جمع بين الأمر والشيء ، وبين النهي عن ضده للمبالغة ، كما تقول : صل قرابتك ولا تقطعهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r7.claim: Al-Razi rejects the claim that the prohibition alone entails the command: some might regard all commerce as inseparable from fraud, so the positive command clarifies that trade is permitted when rights are fulfilled.
RAZI-FULL:v18p34/r7.anchor: لأنه يجوز أن ينهى عن التنقيص وينهى أيضا عن أصل المعاملة
